memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses went out and spoke these words to all Israel: 'I am now a hundred and twenty years old and I am no longer able to lead you. The Lord has said to me, "You shall not cross the Jordan."'" — Deut 31:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses, now a hundred and twenty years old, speaks with remarkable honesty: "I am no longer able to lead you." After forty years of carrying Israel through the wilderness, the great leader acknowledges his limits. His time was ending, and he would not enter the promised land himself. There is something deeply humble and tender in this admission. Even the mightiest servants of God are mortal, and their strength eventually runs out.

There is wisdom for us in Moses' honesty. We live in a world that struggles to accept its own limits, that fears growing older and weaker. But Moses shows us how to face the end of a season, or the end of our strength, with grace — not clinging, not despairing, but entrusting the future to God.

Our abilities fade. Health declines. Seasons of usefulness pass. This is not failure; it is simply the truth of being human. And it need not frighten us, because God's work does not depend on any one of us. Moses would not cross the Jordan, yet God's purposes would march on without pause.

This points us to a comforting truth: God's plans never rest on the strength of one frail person. They rest on Him. Even when our own strength runs out, His never does. The God who sustained Israel through Moses would sustain them still. And for us, whatever our limits, we serve a God whose power is made perfect in our weakness (2 Cor 12:9). Entrust your limits to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do I respond to my own limits and the passing of seasons?
2. Can I entrust the future to God rather than clinging to control?
3. Where do I need to remember that God's power is perfect in my weakness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I am limited and my strength runs out, but Yours never does. Help me face my weaknesses with grace, entrusting the future to You. Be my strength when I have none. Amen.
